newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES STOP GIANTS' WINNING STREAK.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES STOP GIANTS' WINNING STREAK.

text.p: Greg Maddux pitched six scoreless innings before leaving with a recurring hamstring injury as the Atlanta Braves beat San Francisco 4-0 snapping the Giants' nine-game winning streak on Tuesday.
Maddux (2-1) allowed four hits, struck out eight and walked one. He had been scratched from his last scheduled start with a strained right hamstring and appeared to aggravate the injury on Tuesday.
Maddux has not allowed an earned run in his last 24 innings and lowered his ERA to 1.33.
Kenny Lofton had two hits and scored twice for the Braves.
At Colorado, Roger Bailey tossed a six-hitter and Larry Walker went 4-for-5 to lead a 19-hit attack as the Colorado Rockies routed the Florida Marlins 13-4.
Bailey (3-0) walked one and struck out three.
Walker, one of four Rockies to drive in two runs, had his 16th career four-hit game, fourth of the season and second in a row. Every Colorado starter had at least one hit and all but two had an RBI.
Moises Alou belted a pair of two-run homers -- in the seventh and ninth innings -- to account for all of the runs for Florida.
In Los Angeles, Gary Gaetti delivered a two-run double and John Mabry added an RBI double during a three-run ninth as the St. Louis Cardinals rallied for a 6-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Los Angeles closer Todd Worrell (0-2) began the ninth with a 4-3 lead, but blew his first save of the season.
John Frascatore (1-1) pitched a scoreless inning for the victory and Dennis Eckersley worked a 1-2-3 ninth for his fourth save.
In Montreal, Dustin Hermanson allowed one run in five innings and Doug Strange hit a two-run homer as the Montreal Expos defeated the Chicago Cubs, 5-1.
Hermanson, starting for the first time in his professional career, gave up four hits and a walk with four strikeouts.
Omar Daal, Lee Smith and Ugueth Urbina combined for four innings of scoreless relief for the Expos.
In New York, Rick Reed allowed two runs and Edgardo Alfonzo had a three-run double in the fourth inning as the New York Mets cruised to a 7-2 victory over the struggling Cincinnati Reds.
"It seemed like all my pitches were working," Reed said. "I didn't put any pressure on myself. I felt stronger as the game went on."
In San Diego, Shane Reynolds pitched eight strong innings and James Mouton knocked in three runs as the Houston Astros routed the San Diego Padres 12-3 for their third straight win.
Reynolds, who has pitched at least eight innings in each of his last three starts, allowed seven hits and three runs. The right-hander improved to 5-3 lifetime against Padres.
"It's tougher than it looks sometimes," Reynolds said. "The guys played real good defence behind me and we were able to score some runs."
Jeff Bagwell went 3-for-5 with his fourth homer of the season, a double and a single. Derek Bell also had three hits and drove in two runs for the Astros.
